newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mainly flat, fuel oil weaker.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mainly flat, fuel oil weaker.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were flat on Wednesday, apart from weaker fuel oil.
Gas oil held firm in a modestly active day. Traders said Russian premiums could strengthen as supply tightens on increased local agricultural demand for fuel.
Russian material was pegged at high fob quotes +$4 on the offer side. A 50kt May 5-10 Constanza cargo, likely to head eastwards, was not actively offered yet, brokers said.
Italian 0.2 pct material was talked around high fob quotes +$3.50-4.
Diesel was assessed around fob high EN590 quotes +$2-3.
Gasoline was flat to slightly weaker although traders saw fair demand out of Italy ahead of two upcoming long weekends, and a bit of demand out of Eastern Europe.
Naphtha was flat to slightly weaker. Some traders said a decision by Sonatrach to block the loading of double stem naphtha cargoes out of Skikda could weigh on the market.
The arbitrage door to the East only works for double stem cargoes, so a number of cargoes originally earmarked for Asian destinations may now stay put in Europe.
Players did not know how long this policy would last.

The Med fuel oil market was messy, with material thought to be leaving the region now potentially staying. High sulphur kept falling after Tuesday's tumble, losing $1 to around $75/$76 fob, with May swaps down to $74 fob.
A cargo of Spanish material held by a Swiss trader was heard sold to a German trader for delivery into Genoa at $86.50.
Other material said available proved difficult for buyers to pin down. Solid barrels were seen mid-May out of Italy.
The Portugese tender was rumoured to have been won by a local refiner, which would further weaken already poor demand, traders said.
